messages:
Maya S.: morning — starting intake for a new bring-up: `axiom-7b-q4` (4-bit quant). Main ask: canonical prompt/chat templates + API integration examples (tool calling + structured JSON output). Also seeing small quality regressions on codegen tests after q4 conversion, need prioritization checklist and quick eval plan.

Jon R.: can you paste a failing example? quick ones help. I saw drift on the unit-test generation metric yesterday.

Maya S.: failing prompt snippet: `Write a pytest for function that flattens nested dicts.` model often omits edge cases (empty dicts, None). Short repro attached below.

Jon R.: thanks. two quick notes: (1) try system prompt that explicitly enumerates edge cases, (2) compare responses with a structured-output schema so diffs are easier.

Priya K.: sharing the chat template we use for stability testing — short and conservative. you can start with this and tweak:
```
System: You are a precise assistant. Always return JSON matching the schema specified by the user. If unsure, ask clarifying questions.
User: "Task: <natural language prompt>. Output_schema: {\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"tests\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"input\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"expected\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}}}"
Assistant: -> produce JSON only
```

Alex T.: for tool calling, use our function-style call pattern so downstream eval harness can run generated tests automatically. Example (pseudo):
```
Assistant calls: run_test_generator({\"language\":\"python\", \"prompt\": \"Write pytest for flatten_dict\"})
Response: {\"name\":\"run_test_generator\", \"arguments\": {\"files\": [\"tests/test_flatten.py\"]}}
```
We then run the file and capture pass/fail.

Sam L.: on quantization: run parallel evals at q8_q4 combo (8-bit for attention, 4-bit for weights) + full fp16 baseline. Metrics to compute: pass@k for code tasks, BLEU/ROUGE for docs, instruction-following rating % (human or proxy scorer). Prioritize unit-test pass rate and flakiness.

Priya K.: add automated regression gate: if unit-test pass rate drops >3% vs baseline on the canary set, block rollout. Also store diffs per prompt in the eval bucket.

Maya S.: good. can someone post the exact JSON schema we'll require for structured outputs (so model returns can be validated automatically)?

Jon R.: use a minimal schema we already have:
```
{
  \"type\": \"object\",
  \"properties\": {
    \"result\": {\"type\": \"string\"},
    \"tests\": {\"type\": \"array\", \"items\": {\"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": {\"input\": {\"type\": \"string\"}, \"expected\": {\"type\": \"string\"}, \"notes\": {\"type\": \"string\"}}}},
    \"metadata\": {\"type\": \"object\"}
  },
  \"required\": [\"tests\"]
}
```
We validate with `jsonschema` before running. Put failures into the regression bucket.

Priya K.: also include a short prompt prefix to force single-shot vs few-shot behavior depending on the task. e.g., `Example: ...` for few-shot.

Sam L.: for prioritization: triage by impact * probability. High impact = customer-facing codegen or evals used in autop-run, probability = observed regression magnitude in quick q4 trials. I can run a 1k prompt sweep overnight.

Alex T.: small integration tip — in the API layer, expose a `schema_check` flag that validates before returning 200. If failed, return structured error: `{\"error\":\"schema_mismatch\", \"details\": ...}` so callers can fallback to a simpler model.

Maya S.: perfect. next steps: (1) Priya / Jon to finalize schema and chat template, (2) Sam to run quant sweep (8/4 vs fp16) overnight, (3) Alex to add `schema_check` toggle to canary route, (4) I'll prepare canary prompt set and regression buckets.

Priya K.: on it — will push templates to `gitlab.com/redwood/axiom-evals/prompts` and drop a link here when done.

Sam L.: starting sweep now, will post a short summary + perf table tomorrow morning. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for `axiom-7b-q4` in dedicated-us-east-1 — canary-id `canary-20260301-17`

Maya S.: thanks team. tagging @Sam L. and @Priya K. for updates. :thumbsup:
